svg.title: BoE loan-level data tape: generation and testing
svg.desc: Loan data in BoE template coding passes pool data-quality checks and a currency check, the tape is built and validated in memory, written in an accepted format, read back and tested against every rule, and only then released with its cover sheet, report and provenance. The rules come from a dated data set and the field dictionary built from the Bank's template.
svg.text: BoE loan-level data tape: generation and testing
Every rule from data: the field dictionary built from the Bank's template, and a dated rules data set. A rule change is a data change.
Field dictionary
233 AR fields: names, priority,
formats, lengths, code lists
built from the Bank's template
workbook (April 2024)
Tape rules data set
16 BoE rules, each with the
template instruction it comes from;
11 model checks, marked as such
dated: a new template is a new
version, the old one archived
Loan data in BoE template coding
one row per loan, AR1-AR236 codes, Parquet from source to tape
source systems → curated store; data not collected stays blank
Pool data quality (at generation)
template rules · integrity (counts, unique ids, key fields, balances)
plausibility against BoE lending statistics (LTV, income multiples, mix)
a tape can pass every format rule and still be economically wrong
Currency integrity (cash-flow engine load)
every loan's AR65 decodes to the deal currency: GBP only, for now
no FX in the engine, so a mixed pool is refused before any cash flow
Build the tape, validate in memory
template fields only, template order; AR1 = run date; AR2 = pool id
RMBS: origination and maturity as quarter dates; nothing re-coded
a bad value stops the tape: fix it at source, never repair it here
Write the submission file
CSV, tab-delimited TXT or a one-sheet XLSX; split above 150MB
header row: AR codes only; no password; internal columns kept apart
Post-generation tests: read the files back
files: format, size, one sheet, no password, UTF-8, header, parts
content: every loan once; every value equals the pool; totals to the penny
full template validation again, on what was read back
cover sheet agrees with the tape; currency on every loan and the cover
every rule must have a check: a rule with none fails the run
all pass
Release
tape + cover sheet + test report (each rule, its source, its result)
run provenance: code, config and data hashes; each file's SHA-256
Stop
no tape released; the report
names each failed rule
fail
rules applied
at every step
Monthly reporting refreshes the tape each payment date and puts it through the same steps 4 to 7.
Illustrative architecture; synthetic data. Not a statement of the Bank's requirements beyond those cited in the rules data set.
